title: Access Control — User Manual
summary: How to register Hikvision ISAPI door controllers, manage doors and credentials, and review the access event log.

sections.body:
Overview

Access Control manages physical door controllers over the Hikvision ISAPI protocol, across three tabs: Devices & Doors, Credentials, and Event Log. This is a real hardware integration — actions here talk directly to the physical controller, not a simulation.

Key Features

  • Devices & Doors — register a controller by IP/port and credentials, run Test Connection (ISAPI) to confirm it's reachable, then add its doors. Each door can be remotely opened or closed from here.
  • Credentials — provision an access card/employee number to a door with an optional valid-from/valid-to window. Provisioning calls the physical controller first; the local record is only saved if the controller accepts it, so the app never drifts ahead of what the hardware actually has enrolled.
  • Event Log — access events (opens, closes, denied attempts) pulled from the controller. The app doesn't expose a public webhook for the controller to push to — instead, use Sync Now on a device to pull its latest events on demand.

Step-by-Step

  1. In Devices & Doors, click Add Device and enter the controller's name, IP address, port, username, and password. Optionally set its Location (shared with Assets, Stock, and NVRs/Cameras).
  2. Run Test Connection (ISAPI) to confirm the app can reach the controller before relying on it.
  3. Add the physical doors wired to that controller.
  4. In Credentials, provision a card or employee number to a door, with an optional validity window.
  5. Use the remote open/close controls on a door when needed, and Sync Now in Event Log to pull its latest access history.

Tips

  • Access Control currently supports a simple valid-from/valid-to credential window — Hikvision's more advanced day/time access schedules (RightPlan) aren't exposed yet.
  • A failed Test Connection almost always means the IP, port, or credentials are wrong — double-check them against the controller's own web admin page before troubleshooting further.
